import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Set style for better aesthetics
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure with two subplots
# sharey=False is used because Sleep Duration and Quality of Sleep have different scales
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(18, 7), sharey=False)

# --- Plot 1: Sleep Duration Distribution by Occupation ---

# Calculate median sleep duration for each occupation to order the plot
median_sleep_duration = df.groupby('Occupation')['Sleep Duration'].median().sort_values(ascending=False)
ordered_occupations_duration = median_sleep_duration.index

# Create violin plot for Sleep Duration
sns.violinplot(x='Occupation', y='Sleep Duration', data=df, ax=axes[0], palette='viridis', order=ordered_occupations_duration)
axes[0].set_title('Distribution of Sleep Duration by Occupation', fontsize=14)
axes[0].set_xlabel('Occupation', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_ylabel('Sleep Duration (Hours)', fontsize=12)
axes[0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45) # Rotate x-axis labels for readability

# --- Plot 2: Quality of Sleep Distribution by Occupation ---

# Calculate median quality of sleep for each occupation to order the plot
median_quality_of_sleep = df.groupby('Occupation')['Quality of Sleep'].median().sort_values(ascending=False)
ordered_occupations_quality = median_quality_of_sleep.index

# Create violin plot for Quality of Sleep
sns.violinplot(x='Occupation', y='Quality of Sleep', data=df, ax=axes[1], palette='plasma', order=ordered_occupations_quality)
axes[1].set_title('Distribution of Quality of Sleep by Occupation', fontsize=14)
axes[1].set_xlabel('Occupation', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10 Scale)', fontsize=12)
axes[1].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45) # Rotate x-axis labels for readability

# Add an overall title to the figure
fig.suptitle('Impact of Occupation on Key Sleep Health Metrics', fontsize=16, y=1.02)

# Adjust layout to prevent overlapping titles/labels and make space for suptitle
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.95])

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
